evidence: pam-logins-through-winbind / templates/openvpn/pam_winbind.conf.erb:30: require_membership_of = <comma_separated_groups> makes login depend on group membership; the probe runs the login PAM stack with pamtester: p8testvpnin (in p8testgroup) with its password rc=0, wrong password and p8testvpnout (outside the group) refused, while wbinfo -a shows the DC accepts p8testvpnout's password, so the refusal is the membership rule the line declares

pam-winbind-requires-the-group-and-openvpn-pam-installed / files/openvpn/openvpn_pam (whole file, sha256 e664b2eb0c14...): the manifest (lines 58-65) installs that file as /etc/pam.d/openvpn by source; the probe compares the node file's sha256 to exactly that digest

pam-winbind-requires-the-group-and-openvpn-pam-installed / manifests/openvpn_domain.pp:14-15: each group is prefixed with NetBIOS name + separator and joined with commas; with the fixture (P8TEST, '+', [p8testgroup]) that yields 'P8TEST+p8testgroup', which the probe greps as the exact require_membership_of line

purpose gap: Tested: smb.conf domain-member lines (security, netbios name, realm, wins server, workgroup, separator), the join (net rpc testjoin with a P8NOPE mismatch, and the DC listing PUPPET8NODE$), user/group resolution through nsswitch+winbind (id p8testuser@P8TEST.example, p8nouser mismatch), pam_winbind's require_membership_of and /etc/pam.d/openvpn byte for byte, login through the login PAM service (member accepted, wrong password and non-member refused, DC accepting the non-member's password), Kerberos realms against the DC (kinit in P8TEST.EXAMPLE granted, default realm P8TEST.example refused), and WINS host resolution of the DC's NetBIOS name (p8nohost mismatch). Left out, lab-exercisable and not in the outcomes table: templates/openvpn/smb.conf.erb:19 'winbind use default domain = yes' — its observable effect is that domain users resolve and log in by their UNQUALIFIED name (p8testvpnin, not P8TEST+p8testvpnin), which is the name a VPN user types (openvpn_server.pp:168-169 username_as_common_name + pam through login). Every resolution and login probe uses a qualified form (p8testuser@P8TEST.example, 'P8TEST+p8testvpnin'), which works with or without that line, so the setting is untested; the lab can exercise it with the same peer and fixture users (e.g. id -nG p8testvpnin and pamtester login p8testvpnin). Outcome 1 cites smb.conf.erb wholesale but no outcome states this effect; no uncovered row lists it.
